mainTopic: What is included when a field is sold, given, inherited, taken from a גר, or consecrated, and why a sale includes less than a gift.
overview: The amud opens with a short line, איפכא מתנינן לה, that finishes the earlier discussion by learning the ברייתא in reverse. Then a new משנה teaches that selling a field does not include the בור, the גת or the שובך. רבי עקיבא and חכמים argue about whether the seller must buy a path to reach them, and their positions flip when the items themselves are sold to someone else. The משנה limits these exclusions to a sale. A gift, brothers dividing an estate, taking hold of a גר's property, and (for חכמים) הקדש all include the whole field. The גמרא asks why a sale differs from a gift and concludes that the buyer should have spelled out the extras, while a gift recipient could not be expected to. מר זוטרא and רב אשי then disagree about a gift of a 'house holding 100 barrels' that actually holds 120. Finally, רב הונא begins explaining the הקדש clause by contrasting the rules about trees and land, and his statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing the earlier discussion by reversing the text
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the previous problem by saying the ברייתא should be learned the other way around.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the previous discussion. The גמרא fixes a problem by saying we learn the ברייתא with the opinions swapped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion compared a ruling of רבא with a ברייתא in which דייני גולה and דייני ארץ ישראל disagreed. By swapping who said what, the גמרא makes the ברייתא match the ruling of רבא, so there is no longer a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: The reverse, the other way around
We learn it (this is how we recite the text)

phrases.english: We learn it the other way around.
phrases.notes: In our version, the two groups of judges in the ברייתא are swapped, so it fits רבא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a discussion that began before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual reversal: swap the opinions in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא as usually recited seemed to contradict רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read with the opinions reversed, the ברייתא agrees with רבא.

steps.title: Cistern, winepress and dovecote are not sold with the field
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that the בור, גת and שובך are not part of a field sale. רבי עקיבא says the seller must buy a path to reach them, and חכמים say he need not.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: [One who sells a field has sold] neither the cistern, nor the winepress, nor the dovecote, whether they are ruined or in use. And the seller must buy himself a path; these are the words of רבי עקיבא. And the חכמים say: he does not need to.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says the בור, גת and שובך stay with the seller, and records an argument about whether he has to buy a path through the buyer's field to reach them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees these items are not part of the field itself, so they remain the seller's. The argument is only about access. רבי עקיבא holds that a seller gives generously (מוכר בעין יפה), so he even gave away the path and must buy it back. חכמים hold that he kept a path along with the items he kept.

keyTerms.meaning: A cistern or pit dug in the ground
A winepress
A dovecote (a structure for raising doves)
Ruined/abandoned vs. in working use
To buy himself a path (a right of passage)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main question of the whole משנה: when items are held back from a sale, does the right to reach them go with them?

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ לֹא אֶת הַבּוֹר וְלֹא אֶת הַגַּת
phrases.english: MISHNA: Neither the cistern nor the winepress
phrases.notes: This continues the earlier משנה about selling a field: the sale doesn't include these things.

phrases.english: nor the dovecote
whether they are ruined or in use.
And he must buy himself a path,
phrases.notes: He means the seller, who needs to cross the buyer's field to reach what he kept.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.
And the Rabbis say: he does not need to.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ לֹא אֶת הַבּוֹר וְלֹא אֶת הַגַּת וְלֹא אֶת הַשּׁוֹבָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins; it is not connected to step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בור, גת and שובך are not included in a field sale. רבי עקיבא says the seller must buy a path; חכמים say he need not.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא agrees when the seller said 'apart from these'
steps.stepSummary: If the seller wrote 'חוץ מאלו', even רבי עקיבא agrees he does not need to buy a path.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא agrees that when he said to him, 'apart from these,' he does not need to buy himself a path.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה limits רבי עקיבא's opinion. When the seller clearly said he was keeping these items, רבי עקיבא agrees with חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The items would have stayed with the seller even if he said nothing. So when he bothered to say 'חוץ מאלו', it shows he meant to keep something extra, namely the path to reach them.

keyTerms.meaning: And he agrees (concedes)
Apart from these (an explicit exclusion)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva agrees
that when he said to him, 'apart from these,'
he does not need to buy himself a path.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בִּזְמַן שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ חוּץ מֵאֵלּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רבי עקיבא's ruling from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the seller explicitly says 'חוץ מאלו', he keeps the path as well, even according to רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: When the items themselves are sold to someone else
steps.stepSummary: If the owner keeps the field and sells the בור and גת to another person, the positions flip. רבי עקיבא says the buyer needs no path, and חכמים say he must buy one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he sold them to another, רבי עקיבא says: he does not need to buy himself a path. And the חכמים say: he must buy himself a path.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to the opposite case: now the cistern and winepress are what is being sold. It records that רבי עקיבא and חכמים switch sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides stay consistent. For רבי עקיבא a seller gives generously, so the buyer of the cistern gets a path along with it. For חכמים a seller gives only what he must, so the buyer has to buy the path separately.

keyTerms.meaning: He sold them (the items) to another person

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי עקיבא changed his mind. In both cases he favors the buyer, because a seller gives generously. Only the outcome looks reversed, because now the 'buyer' is the one who wants the cistern.

phrases.english: If he sold them to another,
phrases.notes: He kept the field and sold the cistern and winepress themselves to a different person.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לִיקַּח לוֹ דֶּרֶךְ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: he does not need to buy himself a path,

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: צָרִיךְ לִיקַּח לוֹ דֶּרֶךְ.
phrases.english: and the Rabbis say: he must buy himself a path.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same argument to the reverse case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the items are sold and the field is kept, רבי עקיבא says the buyer gets a path free and חכמים say he must buy one.

steps.title: These exclusions apply only to a sale, not to a gift
steps.stepSummary: The משנה limits all of these exclusions to a sale. Someone who gives a field as a gift gives all of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When are these words said? With a seller. But one who gives a gift gives all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks when these rules apply and answers: only with a sale. A gift includes everything in the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who gives a gift is giving generously, so we assume he did not hold back the cistern or the winepress. A seller, by contrast, includes only what is plainly part of the field.

keyTerms.meaning: When are these words said? (a phrase that sets a limit on a rule)
One who gives a gift
All of it

phrases.english: When are these words said?
phrases.notes: He means the rule that these items are left out of the field.

phrases.english: With a seller, but with one who gives a gift
he gives all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the exclusions of step 2 to a sale.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The exclusions apply only to a sale. A gift includes the whole field with everything in it.

steps.title: Brothers dividing an estate and taking a convert's property
steps.stepSummary: Brothers who divide an inheritance, and someone who takes ownerless property of a גר, each acquire the whole field, including the items a sale would leave out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Brothers who divided: if they acquired a field, they acquired all of it. One who takes possession of a גר's property: if he took possession of a field, he took possession of all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds two more cases that work like a gift. In both, the whole field is acquired, cistern and winepress included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When brothers split an estate, each one gets his portion in full, not under the narrow rules of a sale. A גר who dies without heirs leaves ownerless property. Whoever takes hold of a field from it (מחזיק) gets the whole field, because no seller is holding anything back.

keyTerms.meaning: Brothers who divided (their father's estate)
One who takes possession (acquires by an act of ownership)
The property of a convert (ownerless when he dies without heirs)

phrases.english: Brothers who divided,
if they acquired a field, they acquired all of it.
One who takes possession of the property of a convert,
phrases.notes: A convert who dies with no heirs leaves property that belongs to no one, so the first to take hold of it gets it.

phrases.english: if he took possession of a field, he took possession of all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאַחִין שֶׁחָלְקוּ זָכוּ בַּשָּׂדֶה זָכוּ בְּכוּלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more cases that follow the gift rule from step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Brothers dividing an estate, and one who takes possession of a גר's property, acquire the entire field, including the items that a sale would leave out.

steps.title: Consecrating a field: all of it, or only a little more?
steps.stepSummary: חכמים rule that one who is מקדיש a field includes everything in it. רבי שמעון says that, beyond the field itself, only the grafted carob and the sycamore trunk become הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who consecrates a field has consecrated all of it. רבי שמעון says: one who consecrates a field has consecrated, of the extra items, only the grafted carob tree and the sycamore trunk.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a last case to its list: giving a field to הקדש. חכמים and רבי שמעון disagree about how much is included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like a gift, הקדש is done generously, so according to חכמים it includes everything, even items a sale would leave out. רבי שמעון disagrees: of all those extra items, only the grafted carob and the sycamore trunk go to הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: One who gives something to the בית המקדש (makes it holy property)
A grafted carob tree
The trunk of a sycamore tree that has been cut back

steps.whatToRemember: Gift, inheritance, הפקר of a גר, and (for חכמים) הקדש all include the whole field. Only a sale leaves out the extra items.

phrases.aramaic: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה – הִקְדִּישׁ אֶת כּוּלָּהּ.
phrases.english: One who consecrates the field has consecrated all of it.
Rabbi Shimon says:
One who consecrates the field

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִקְדִּישׁ אֶלָּא אֶת הֶחָרוּב הַמּוּרְכָּב,
phrases.english: has consecrated only the grafted carob tree,
phrases.notes: He means: of all the extra items that a sale leaves out, only these two go to הקדש.

phrases.english: and the sycamore trunk.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה – הִקְדִּישׁ אֶת כּוּלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds הקדש to the list of transfers that include the whole field, with רבי שמעון disagreeing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to חכמים, הקדש includes the whole field. רבי שמעון says it includes only the grafted carob and sycamore trunk beyond the field.

steps.title: Why is a sale different from a gift?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the real difference is between a sale and a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is different about a sale, and what is different about a gift?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks why the משנה gives the buyer less than the gift recipient. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the owner said the same thing: 'this field.' So why does a buyer lose the extra items while a gift recipient gets them? The גמרא wants a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
What is the difference?
A sale
A gift

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is different about a sale,
and what is different about a gift?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא מֶכֶר וּמַאי שְׁנָא מַתָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the משנה's split between sale and gift.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logical reason a sale leaves out items that a gift includes.

steps.title: יהודה בן נקוסא: one specified, one did not
steps.stepSummary: יהודה בן נקוסא explains to רבי that the seller 'specified' and the giver did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהודה בן נקוסא explained before רבי: this one specified, and that one did not specify.
steps.whatsHappening: An answer is offered: the difference comes from what each owner spelled out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His claim is that the seller made clear he was keeping the extra items, while the giver said nothing, so everything passed. The next step will question whether that describes the case at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Spelled out, specified
A sage of the time of רבי

phrases.aramaic: פֵּירֵשׁ יְהוּדָה בֶּן נְקוֹסָא לִפְנֵי רַבִּי:
phrases.english: Yehuda ben Nekosa explained before Rabbi:
phrases.notes: רבי here is רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: This one specified, and that one did not specify.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the seller and 'that one' is the giver.

steps.triggerLanguage: פֵּירֵשׁ יְהוּדָה בֶּן נְקוֹסָא לִפְנֵי רַבִּי
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The seller specified what he kept, and the giver did not.

steps.title: But nobody specified anything
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: in the משנה's cases neither the seller nor the giver specified anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: This 'this one specified and that one did not specify'?! This one did not specify, and that one did not specify!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 9. In the משנה, both owners just said 'the field' and nothing more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the seller had really spelled out what he was keeping, there would be no question at all. The משנה is about a plain sale with no details, so 'specifying' cannot be the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: This (here: 'how can you say this?')

phrases.english: This: 'this one specified and that one did not specify'?!

phrases.aramaic: זֶה לֹא פֵּירֵשׁ וְזֶה לֹא פֵּירֵשׁ הוּא!
phrases.english: This one did not specify, and that one did not specify!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי זֶה פֵּירֵשׁ וְזֶה לֹא פֵּירֵשׁ
steps.kashyaTarget: יהודה בן נקוסא's claim that the seller specified
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's case has no specifying by anyone, so that cannot be what separates sale from gift.

steps.title: The buyer should have specified; the receiver could not
steps.stepSummary: The answer is rephrased: the buyer should have demanded the extra items in writing, but a gift recipient would not be expected to make demands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: this one should have specified, and that one should not have specified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the answer. The point is not what was said, but who was expected to speak up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A buyer is paying, so he should have made sure the extra items were written in. Since he did not, he loses them. A gift recipient cannot fairly set conditions on a gift, so his silence does not hurt him and he gets everything.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a corrected answer)
He should have specified

steps.confusionAlert: In step 9, 'this one' meant the seller. Here 'this one' means the buyer, the one who should have spoken up. The focus moves from the owner to the person receiving the field.
steps.whatToRemember: A sale leaves out the extras because the buyer should have asked for them. A gift includes them because the receiver could not be expected to ask.

phrases.english: Rather, this one should have specified,
phrases.notes: Here 'this one' is the buyer, who should have made sure the extras were written in.

phrases.english: and that one should not have specified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by restating יהודה בן נקוסא's idea correctly.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference was about which owner actually spelled things out.
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference is about which receiver was expected to spell things out: the buyer was, the gift recipient was not.

steps.title: A gift of a 'house holding 100 barrels' that holds 120
steps.stepSummary: A man told people to give someone a house holding 100 barrels, and the house turned out to hold 120.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man said to them: 'Give so-and-so a house that holds 100 barrels.' It turned out that it held 120.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real case about the size of a gift. This sets up מר זוטרא's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that a gift is read generously. Here the giver named a measure, 100 barrels, but the house is bigger. The question is whether the receiver gets the whole house or only what was described.

keyTerms.meaning: So-and-so
Barrels (large jugs)
It turned out, it was found

phrases.english: There was a certain man who said to them:
'Give so-and-so a house
that holds 100 barrels.'
It turned out that it held 120.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the general rule of gifts to a case where the giver set a measure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: the gift was described as 100 barrels, but the house holds 120.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: he gets only what was said
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא rules that the giver said 100, not 120, so the receiver gets only the 100-barrel portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: He told him 100; he did not tell him 120.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא gives his ruling on the case. The receiver is limited to the measure the giver named.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For מר זוטרא, even though a gift is read generously, a clear number limits it. The giver said '100 barrels,' so the extra space that holds 20 more stays with the giver.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who rules on the case
One hundred and twenty

steps.whyThisMatters: According to מר זוטרא, the 'generous gift' rule has a limit: the giver's own clear words decide how much is given. רב אשי disagrees in the next step.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
He said 100 to him,
he did not say 120 to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the case set up in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The receiver gets only the part of the house that holds 100 barrels, since that is what the giver said.

steps.title: רב אשי: A gift-giver gives generously, so the receiver gets the whole house
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי disagrees with מר זוטרא. He points to the משנה, which says a seller holds back the extra items but a gift-giver gives everything. This shows that a giver gives generously, so the receiver should get the entire house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Didn't we learn in the משנה, 'When does this apply? To a seller. But one who gives a gift gives all of them'? So a person who gives a gift gives generously. Here too, a person who gives a gift gives generously.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the opposite ruling from מר זוטרא in the 100-barrel house case. He backs it up with our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא read the giver's words exactly: 100 barrels means 100 barrels. רב אשי says the משנה already teaches that a gift-giver gives with a generous spirit (עין יפה). So we should not read his words stingily, and the receiver gets the whole house, even though it holds 120.

keyTerms.meaning: Didn't we learn (in a משנה)? An opening that brings a proof from a known source
In what case is this said? It limits a rule to certain cases
So we see / apparently. It draws a conclusion
With a 'good eye': generously
Here too. It applies the rule to the current case

steps.whatToRemember: מר זוטרא: the receiver gets only what was said (100 barrels). רב אשי: a gift-giver gives generously, so the receiver gets the whole house.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not proving a new rule about selling. He takes the משנה's gift rule (giver gives everything) and applies it to the house case to argue against מר זוטרא.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Didn't we learn (in the mishna):
In what case is this said? With a seller,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּנוֹתֵן מַתָּנָה – נוֹתֵן אֶת כּוּלָּן?
phrases.english: but one who gives a gift gives all of them?
So we see that one who gives a gift
gives generously;
here too, one who gives a gift
gives generously.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר, מִי לָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ruling opposite to מר זוטרא's in step 13, supported by the משנה
steps.raayaObject: In the 100-barrel house case, the receiver gets the entire house
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: a seller does not include extra items, but a gift-giver gives all of them, which shows a giver gives generously

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: one who consecrates a field consecrates everything
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: one who is מקדיש a field has consecrated all of it. This sets up a new discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who consecrates a field has consecrated (all of it), etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the משנה about הקדש. It is setting up רב הונא's teaching, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that a person who gives a field to הקדש includes everything in it, the same way as a gift-giver. רב הונא is about to explain how far this goes, especially with trees.

keyTerms.meaning: One who consecrates property to the Temple treasury (הקדש)
Etc.: the rest of the משנה's line is assumed

phrases.english: One who consecrates the field
has consecrated, etc.
phrases.notes: The full line in the משנה says he has consecrated all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the gift discussion and opens the משנה's הקדש clause
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who consecrates a field consecrates all of it

steps.title: רב הונא begins: the רבנן's rules about two trees and land
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא starts his teaching by recalling the רבנן's rules. A buyer of two trees in someone else's field does not get any land. A seller who sells land but keeps two trees for himself does keep land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Even though the רבנן said that one who buys two trees in another's field does not acquire land, and one who sells land and keeps two trees for himself keeps land...
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא opens with the words 'even though.' He lists the רבנן's rules first, setting up a contrast he will make about הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן's two rules both lean against the receiver. The buyer of two trees gets no ground, while the seller who keeps two trees does keep ground. 'Even though' signals that רב הונא will say something different for one who consecrates.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though. It introduces a contrast
Trees
Land / ground
He kept back / retained for himself

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the two directions. The buyer of two trees does NOT get land, but the seller who keeps two trees DOES keep land.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Even though the Rabbis said:

phrases.aramaic: הַקּוֹנֶה שְׁנֵי אִילָנוֹת בְּתוֹךְ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ –
phrases.english: One who buys two trees inside another's field
has not acquired land,

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר קַרְקַע וְשִׁיֵּיר שְׁנֵי אִילָנוֹת לְפָנָיו –
phrases.english: if he sold land and kept two trees for himself,
he has land.
phrases.notes: He keeps the ground around those trees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins רב הונא's explanation of the הקדש line from step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Background rules: a buyer of two trees gets no land, and a seller who keeps two trees keeps land

steps.title: Even רבי עקיבא's 'generous seller' rule is limited to a pit and cistern
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא continues. Even רבי עקיבא, who holds a seller sells generously, only says so for a pit and cistern, which do not weaken the land. Trees do weaken the land. The statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even according to רבי עקיבא, who says a seller sells generously, that applies only to a pit and cistern, which do not weaken the land. But trees, which do weaken the land...
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא adds that even the most generous view of selling has a limit when it comes to trees. The sentence is not finished here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's 'generous seller' idea was said about a pit and cistern, which take nothing from the soil. Trees pull strength from the land, so a seller treats them differently. This sharpens the contrast רב הונא is building toward for הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: A seller sells generously, keeping nothing back (רבי עקיבא's view)
These words apply only... It limits a rule
A pit and a cistern
Weaken the land (drain its strength)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that whether something harms the land changes how generously we read a transfer. This is the key to רב הונא's coming point about הקדש.

phrases.english: And even according to Rabbi Akiva,
who says: a seller sells generously,
these words apply to a pit and a cistern,
which do not weaken the land;
but trees, which do weaken the land,
phrases.notes: The sentence isn't finished; רב הונא's point continues on the next amud.
